paragraphs: Lily borrowed an old magazine from the school library on Thursday. It was full of animals from long ago. She read it in the club hour with Leo. "Write a page for the blog," said Leo, "and I will draw the pictures." That night, Lily wrote Animals of Long Ago. Teacher Kim read the page first, and she smiled.

The Mammoth. Once, mammoths walked on the cold land in the north. A mammoth was like a big elephant with long brown fur. It was much taller than a man, and its fur kept it warm. Its two long white tusks bent up in front. It ate grass and leaves on the hills. Mammoths lived in groups, like elephants today. No mammoth lives today. Mammoths are extinct.

The Cave Bear. The cave bear lived in a cave on a hill. A cave is a good home, because it is dry and quiet. It was as big as the biggest bears of today. It ate plants and fruit, and not much meat. In the cold winter, it slept in its cave for many weeks. Today, people find the old bones of cave bears in dark caves. The bones tell us about this big creature. The cave bear is extinct, too.

Cave Pictures. Long ago, people drew animals on the walls of caves. They used stones and sticks for their colors and lines. They drew mammoths, bears, and horses in red and black. These pictures show us how the creatures looked. Some of the pictures are more than ten thousand years old. Dinosaurs are extinct, too, but they lived much earlier. People never saw a dinosaur.
Mia read the page after school. "Which extinct animal do you want to see?" she asked. "I want to see a mammoth," said Leo. "I drew it in a school hat!" Lily looked at his picture and laughed.
